newsitem.title: DUBAI: First Qatargas condensate cargo sails to China.
newsitem.headline: First Qatargas condensate cargo sails to China.

text.p: A ship to export the first cargo of condensate from the Qatargas liquefied natural gas (LNG) project has left the Qatari port of Ras Laffan for China, the official Qatar News Agency (QNA) reported on Saturday.
It said the vessel carrying 55,000 metric tonnes of condensate left on Friday.
Condensate production from the Qatargas project is forecast to reach 30,000 barrels per day (bpd) by the end of the year, increasing to nearly 50,000 bpd by late 1998.
Qatar's current condensate exports run at some 35,000 bpd.
LNG exports from the multi-billion Qatargas project to Japan are scheduled to start in December, the first LNG shipments from OPEC member Qatar.

Qatar Liquefied Gas Co, or Qatargas, is 65 percent owned by the state Qatar General Petroleum Corp, 10 percent each by U.S. Mobil Corp and France's Total SA, and 7.5 percent each by Japan's Mitsui and Marubeni Corp.
The project is one of three LNG developments in the Gulf Arab state which will exploit the reserves of the North Field, the world's biggest single offshore gas field.
